text: The books of David Hume were banned starting in 1761. Hume was one of the authors all of whose books were added to the Index Librorum Prohibitorum, the official list of books, actively maintained until 1948, that Catholics were forbidden to publish or to read. His Dialogues was published in 1779 without his name as author; when the author was identified, which did not take long, the book was added to the other works by Hume that had been banned.
meta_description: David Hume's books were banned starting in 1761 and added to the Index Librorum Prohibitorum; Dialogues (1779) joined them once he was identified as its author.
